airport.name: Wiley Post Will Rogers Memorial Airport

summary: Wiley Post Will Rogers Memorial Airport (BRW) serves Utqiaġvik, the northernmost community in the United States, located on the Arctic coast of Alaska about 320 miles north of the Arctic Circle. The airport is named in honor of pioneering aviator Wiley Post and humorist Will Rogers, who perished in a plane crash near the area in 1935. As the primary gateway to the North Slope, it plays a vital role in supporting Iñupiat communities, scientific research, and Prudhoe Bay oil operations.
faqs:
Q: Why is the airport named after Wiley Post and Will Rogers?
A: The airport honors the famous aviator Wiley Post and entertainer Will Rogers, who died together in a plane crash near Utqiaġvik (then called Barrow) on August 15, 1935, while exploring the Arctic.

Q: What airlines serve Wiley Post Will Rogers Memorial Airport?
A: Primarily Alaska Airlines operates passenger service to BRW, connecting Utqiaġvik with Anchorage and other Alaskan hubs, along with smaller regional and charter carriers.

Q: How far is the airport from Utqiaġvik town center?
A: The airport is located just a few miles southwest of Utqiaġvik, making it a quick drive or taxi ride from the community center.

Q: Can you see the Northern Lights from the airport?
A: Yes, the airport's location above the Arctic Circle makes it an excellent vantage point for aurora viewing during the long dark polar nights from late autumn through early spring.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available but limited, so booking in advance is strongly recommended for travelers heading into the surrounding tundra. Taxi services and pre-arranged shuttles from local hotels are the most common ways to reach town from the terminal. Be prepared for weather-related flight delays, as fog, wind, and snow can disrupt schedules even in summer months.
local_tip: Bring layered clothing regardless of the season—summer temperatures can hover around 40°F and the strong Arctic wind off the Chukchi Sea makes the tarmac feel significantly colder than reported.
